vocabulary.meaning_en: information about things that are happening now
vocabulary.note_ar: news اسم مفرد غير معدود رغم حرف s: The news is good
vocabulary.note_en: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb: The news is good.
vocabulary.example: I watch the news every evening.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a little afraid or worried
vocabulary.example: I'm nervous before my exam.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the person who is in charge of you at work
vocabulary.example: My boss helps me at work.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something that is true
vocabulary.example: It is a fact that water boils at 100 degrees.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an emotion, like happy, sad or angry
vocabulary.example: Happy and sad are feelings.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to let people see something
vocabulary.note_ar: show لها معنى آخر كاسم: برنامج
vocabulary.note_en: As a noun, show means a TV or radio program.
vocabulary.example: Don't show your feelings when you read the news.

vocabulary.meaning_en: prepared to start
vocabulary.example: Are you ready? Let's start.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a report in the news, or a tale about events
vocabulary.example: Let's read the first story.

vocabulary.meaning_en: liked by many people
vocabulary.example: This book is very popular with children.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a baby duck
vocabulary.example: The duckling is looking for its mother.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not able to find the way; missing
vocabulary.example: The little boy is lost in the market.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not happy
vocabulary.example: This story is very sad.

vocabulary.meaning_en: feeling good and pleased
vocabulary.example: I am very happy for her.

vocabulary.meaning_en: feeling strong and bad about something wrong
vocabulary.example: That makes me very angry.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to be first in a race or game
vocabulary.example: She wins the race.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a competition to see who is fastest
vocabulary.example: A grandmother wins the car race.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who gathers and tells the news
vocabulary.example: She rarely talks to reporters.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not often; almost never
vocabulary.example: She rarely talks to reporters.

vocabulary.meaning_en: many times
vocabulary.example: She often says, 'Nothing can stop me now!'

vocabulary.meaning_en: number one in order
vocabulary.example: Let's try the first story.

vocabulary.meaning_en: number two in order
vocabulary.example: She's reading the second story.

vocabulary.meaning_en: number three in order
vocabulary.example: Let's try the third story.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who works in government
vocabulary.example: City politicians are using city money.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place where you can borrow books
vocabulary.note_ar: لا تخلطها مع bookstore (محل بيع الكتب)
vocabulary.note_en: Not a bookstore: you borrow books, you do not buy them.
vocabulary.example: The money is from the children's library.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a big ship that people travel on for a holiday
vocabulary.example: The cruise ship is very big.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to do or say something again
vocabulary.example: Let's repeat the first story.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a table where you work or study
vocabulary.example: Put your books on the desk.

fine_lines.title: fact vs feeling
fine_lines.explanation_ar: fact شيء صحيح يمكن إثباته (امرأة عمرها 80 فازت بالسباق). feeling شيء نحسّه في داخلنا (أنا سعيد، أنا غاضب). قارئ الأخبار يقول الحقائق فقط.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A fact is something true (an 80-year-old woman wins the race). A feeling is what you feel inside (I'm happy, I'm angry). A news reader gives only facts.

examples.sentence: The book is popular with children.
I am very happy for her.

fine_lines.title: often vs rarely
fine_lines.explanation_ar: often = مرات كثيرة. rarely = مرات قليلة جدًا (تقريبًا أبدًا). كلاهما قبل الفعل العادي.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Often means many times. Rarely means very few times (almost never). Both go before the main verb.

expressions.meaning_en: An informal way to say 'yes, of course'.
expressions.example: Can you help me? - Sure thing.

expressions.meaning_en: Asking if someone can start now.

expressions.phrase: Hello, and welcome to The News.
expressions.meaning_ar: مرحبًا، وأهلًا بكم في نشرة الأخبار.
expressions.meaning_en: A way to start a news program.
expressions.example: Hello, and welcome to the morning show.
Sorry, that's wrong. Let me try again.

expressions.meaning_en: You are making the same mistake again.
expressions.example: Stop! You are doing it again.

expressions.meaning_en: I am thinking of a good plan.
expressions.example: I have an idea. Let's go to the park.

expressions.meaning_en: Tell only the true information, no feelings.
expressions.example: Don't tell me what you think. Just the facts.

expressions.meaning_en: Her good news makes me happy.
expressions.example: My friend passed her exam. I'm very happy for her.

expressions.meaning_en: This causes me to feel angry.
expressions.example: People throw trash in the park. That makes me very angry.
Turn left at the bank. - Okay. I got it.

expressions.meaning_en: Now you are doing it right.
expressions.example: Yes, that's the right answer. Now you've got it!

grammar.title: Adverbs of frequency: always, often, rarely, never
grammar.explanation_ar: 1) ترتيبها من الأكثر للأقل: always (دائمًا) ← often (غالبًا) ← sometimes (أحيانًا) ← rarely (نادرًا) ← never (أبدًا). 2) تأتي قبل الفعل العادي: She rarely talks to reporters. 3) وبعد فعل be: She is often late.
grammar.explanation_en: 1) From most to least: always, often, sometimes, rarely, never. 2) They go before a main verb: She rarely talks to reporters. 3) They go after be: She is often late.
examples: She often says, 'Nothing can stop me now!'

grammar.title: Simple present with he/she/it: add -s
grammar.explanation_ar: في المضارع البسيط مع he و she و it نضيف s للفعل: she talks, she says, he wins. ومع do نقول does: She always does that. وبعض الأفعال نضيف لها es: watch → watches، go → goes.
grammar.explanation_en: In the simple present, add -s to the verb with he, she and it: she talks, she says, he wins. Do becomes does: She always does that. Some verbs add -es: watch → watches, go → goes.
examples: He watches the news every night.
The duckling looks for its mother.

grammar.title: Ordinal numbers: first, second, third
grammar.explanation_ar: الأعداد الترتيبية تقول الترتيب: first (الأول)، second (الثاني)، third (الثالث)، ثم نضيف th: fourth, fifth. ونضع قبلها the غالبًا: the first story.
grammar.explanation_en: Ordinal numbers show order: first, second, third, then add -th: fourth, fifth. We usually use the before them: the first story.
examples: This is the third time I'm trying.

questions.question: Which one is a feeling?
questions.explanation_en: Angry is a feeling; the others are facts.

questions.question: She always ___ that.
questions.explanation_ar: مع she نستخدم does في المضارع البسيط.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: never قبل الفعل، ومع we لا نضيف s.
questions.explanation_en: Never goes before the verb; with we, no -s.

questions.question: A baby duck is a ___.
questions.explanation_en: A duckling is a baby duck.

questions.question: One, two, three -> first, second, ___
questions.explanation_ar: العدد الترتيبي من three هو third.
questions.explanation_en: The ordinal of three is third.

questions.question: A grandmother ___ the car race.
questions.explanation_en: The subject is one person (she), so add -s: wins.

questions.question: 'I'm nervous' means:
questions.explanation_en: Nervous means a little worried or afraid.

questions.question: 'Okay. I got it.' means:
questions.explanation_en: I got it means I understand.

questions.question: Which is the correct order from most to least?
questions.explanation_ar: الترتيب: always ثم often ثم rarely ثم never.
questions.explanation_en: Always, often, rarely, never: from most to least.
